knowledge:
- key_parameters: gene.data=Vector or matrix of gene data (e.g., log2 fold changes, p-values) where names/rownames are gene IDs ;; cpd.data=Vector or matrix of compound/metabolite data where names/rownames are compound IDs ;; pathway.id=Character vector of KEGG pathway IDs (e.g., "04110") ;; species=Character code for the species (e.g., "hsa", "eco", "ko") ;; out.suffix=Suffix added to output files ;; kegg.native=Logical; if TRUE, renders native KEGG PNG; if FALSE, renders Graphviz PDF ;; same.layer=Logical; if TRUE, controls node colors on the original layer; if FALSE, adds an extra layer (useful for replacing labels with official symbols or speeding up rendering) ;; split.group=Logical; if TRUE, splits node groups into individual detached nodes (Graphviz view only) ;; expand.node=Logical; if TRUE, expands multiple-gene nodes into individual genes (Graphviz view only) ;; multi.state=Logical; if TRUE, plots multiple samples/states in one graph (sliced nodes) ;; match.data=Logical; if TRUE, pairs/matches samples between gene.data and cpd.data ;; discrete=List or vector; specifies whether gene or compound data should be treated as discrete ;; limit=List or vector; limits for gene and compound data color scales ;; bins=List or vector; number of bins for gene and compound data color scales
- alternatives: SBGNview=Use when working with other major pathway databases (Reactome, MetaCyc, SMPDB, PANTHER, METACROP, etc.) with more extensive graphics control and sub-pathway highlight ;; gage=Use for pathway and gene set enrichment analysis, which can be piped into pathview for visualization
- when_to_use: Use when integrating transcriptomics, proteomics, metagenomics, or metabolomics data onto KEGG pathway diagrams, comparing multiple experimental states/samples side-by-side on a pathway map, or visualizing both gene expression and metabolite abundance simultaneously on metabolic pathways.
- pitfalls: Installing dependencies like Rgraphviz or XML (KEGGgraph dependency) can be complicated on older R/Bioconductor versions or Windows systems (where XML may need manual installation) ;; Using same.layer = TRUE (default) for native KEGG view keeps original labels but takes longer to compute; same.layer = FALSE is faster but doubles file size and replaces original labels with official symbols ;; When plotting multiple samples separately (multi.state = FALSE), samples in gene.data and cpd.data must be matched/paired, making match.data ineffective ;; KEGG requires subscription for FTP access since May 2011, but pathview bypasses this by downloading individual files via API/HTTP (free for academic/non-commercial use).

workflows.name: gene_data_visualization
workflows.intent: Visualize a single sample of gene expression data on a signaling pathway using both native KEGG and Graphviz layouts.
input: gene_expression.tsv (matrix of log2 fold changes or expression values with Entrez Gene IDs as row names)
workflows.stages: 1. Load package and data ;; 2. Render native KEGG view with default settings ;; 3. Render native KEGG view with two layers (same.layer = FALSE) ;; 4. Render Graphviz view with default settings ;; 5. Render Graphviz view with two layers ;; 6. Render Graphviz view with split node groups ;; 7. Render Graphviz view with expanded multiple-gene nodes
workflows.code:
library(pathview)
data(gse16873.d)
data(demo.paths)
i <- 1
pv.out <- pathview(gene.data = gse16873.d[, 1], pathway.id = demo.paths$sel.paths[i],
                   species = "hsa", out.suffix = "gse16873", kegg.native = T)
pv.out <- pathview(gene.data = gse16873.d[, 1], pathway.id = demo.paths$sel.paths[i],
                   species = "hsa", out.suffix = "gse16873.2layer", kegg.native = T,
                   same.layer = F)
pv.out <- pathview(gene.data = gse16873.d[, 1], pathway.id = demo.paths$sel.paths[i],
                   species = "hsa", out.suffix = "gse16873", kegg.native = F,
                   sign.pos = demo.paths$spos[i])
pv.out <- pathview(gene.data = gse16873.d[, 1], pathway.id = demo.paths$sel.paths[i], 
    species = "hsa", out.suffix = "gse16873.2layer", kegg.native = F, 
    sign.pos = demo.paths$spos[i], same.layer = F)
pv.out <- pathview(gene.data = gse16873.d[, 1], pathway.id = demo.paths$sel.paths[i], 
    species = "hsa", out.suffix = "gse16873.split", kegg.native = F, 
    sign.pos = demo.paths$spos[i], split.group = T)
pv.out <- pathview(gene.data = gse16873.d[, 1], pathway.id = demo.paths$sel.paths[i], 
    species = "hsa", out.suffix = "gse16873.split.expanded", kegg.native = F,
    sign.pos = demo.paths$spos[i], split.group = T, expand.node = T)

workflows.name: integrated_gene_compound_visualization
workflows.intent: Integrate and visualize both gene expression and compound/metabolite data simultaneously on a metabolic pathway.
input: gene_expression.tsv (matrix of gene expression values with Entrez Gene IDs as row names)
metabolite_abundance.tsv (matrix of compound/metabolite values with KEGG compound IDs as row names)
workflows.stages: 1. Load package and data ;; 2. Render native KEGG view with both gene and compound data ;; 3. Render Graphviz view with both gene and compound data
workflows.code:
library(pathview)
data(gse16873.d)
sim.cpd.data=sim.mol.data(mol.type="cpd", nmol=3000)
data(demo.paths)
i <- 3
pv.out <- pathview(gene.data = gse16873.d[, 1], cpd.data = sim.cpd.data, 
    pathway.id = demo.paths$sel.paths[i], species = "hsa", out.suffix = "gse16873.cpd", 
    keys.align = "y", kegg.native = T, key.pos = demo.paths$kpos1[i])
pv.out <- pathview(gene.data = gse16873.d[, 1], cpd.data = sim.cpd.data, 
    pathway.id = demo.paths$sel.paths[i], species = "hsa", out.suffix = "gse16873.cpd", 
    keys.align = "y", kegg.native = F, key.pos = demo.paths$kpos2[i], 
    sign.pos = demo.paths$spos[i], cpd.lab.offset = demo.paths$offs[i])

workflows.name: multi_sample_comparison
workflows.intent: Compare multiple samples or experimental states side-by-side on a single pathway graph by slicing nodes.
input: multi_sample_gene_expression.tsv (matrix of gene expression across multiple samples)
multi_sample_metabolite_abundance.tsv (matrix of metabolite values across multiple samples)
workflows.stages: 1. Load package and multi-sample data ;; 2. Render native KEGG view without sample matching ;; 3. Render native KEGG view with sample matching ;; 4. Render Graphviz view with multi-sample data
workflows.code:
library(pathview)
data(gse16873.d)
sim.cpd.data=sim.mol.data(mol.type="cpd", nmol=3000)
set.seed(10)
sim.cpd.data2 = matrix(sample(sim.cpd.data, 18000, replace = T), ncol = 6)
rownames(sim.cpd.data2) = names(sim.cpd.data)
colnames(sim.cpd.data2) = paste("exp", 1:6, sep = "")
data(demo.paths)
i <- 3
pv.out <- pathview(gene.data = gse16873.d[, 1:3], 
    cpd.data = sim.cpd.data2[, 1:2], pathway.id = demo.paths$sel.paths[i], 
    species = "hsa", out.suffix = "gse16873.cpd.3-2s", keys.align = "y", 
    kegg.native = T, match.data = F, multi.state = T, same.layer = T)
pv.out <- pathview(gene.data = gse16873.d[, 1:3], 
    cpd.data = sim.cpd.data2[, 1:2], pathway.id = demo.paths$sel.paths[i], 
    species = "hsa", out.suffix = "gse16873.cpd.3-2s.match", 
    keys.align = "y", kegg.native = T, match.data = T, multi.state = T, 
    same.layer = T)
pv.out <- pathview(gene.data = gse16873.d[, 1:3], 
    cpd.data = sim.cpd.data2[, 1:2], pathway.id = demo.paths$sel.paths[i], 
    species = "hsa", out.suffix = "gse16873.cpd.3-2s", keys.align = "y", 
    kegg.native = F, match.data = F, multi.state = T, same.layer = T,
    key.pos = demo.paths$kpos2[i], sign.pos = demo.paths$spos[i])

workflows.name: discrete_data_visualization
workflows.intent: Visualize discrete lists of significant genes and compounds on a pathway graph.
workflows.stages: 1. Load package and identify significant genes/compounds ;; 2. Render native KEGG view with discrete color mapping for both genes and compounds ;; 3. Render native KEGG view with discrete mapping for genes and continuous mapping for compounds
workflows.code:
library(pathview)
require(org.Hs.eg.db)
data(gse16873.d)
sim.cpd.data=sim.mol.data(mol.type="cpd", nmol=3000)
data(demo.paths)
i <- 3
gse16873.t <- apply(gse16873.d, 1, function(x) t.test(x, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value)
sel.genes <- names(gse16873.t)[gse16873.t < 0.1]
sel.cpds <- names(sim.cpd.data)[abs(sim.cpd.data) > 0.5]
pv.out <- pathview(gene.data = sel.genes, cpd.data = sel.cpds, 
    pathway.id = demo.paths$sel.paths[i], species = "hsa", out.suffix = "sel.genes.sel.cpd", 
    keys.align = "y", kegg.native = T, key.pos = demo.paths$kpos1[i], 
    limit = list(gene = 5, cpd = 2), bins = list(gene = 5, cpd = 2), 
    na.col = "gray", discrete = list(gene = T, cpd = T))
pv.out <- pathview(gene.data = sel.genes, cpd.data = sim.cpd.data, 
    pathway.id = demo.paths$sel.paths[i], species = "hsa", out.suffix = "sel.genes.cpd",
    keys.align = "y", kegg.native = T, key.pos = demo.paths$kpos1[i], 
    limit = list(gene = 5, cpd = 1), bins = list(gene = 5, cpd = 10), 
    na.col = "gray", discrete = list(gene = T, cpd = F))

workflows.name: id_mapping_and_visualization
workflows.intent: Map non-standard gene (Ensembl) and compound (CAS) IDs to standard KEGG/Entrez IDs and visualize them.
workflows.stages: 1. Load package and non-standard ID data ;; 2. Render pathway using automatic ID mapping inside pathview ;; 3. Perform manual ID mapping using cpdidmap and id2eg ;; 4. Summarize mapped data using mol.sum ;; 5. Render pathway using manually mapped data
workflows.code:
library(pathview)
data(demo.paths)
data(gene.idtype.list)
data(cpd.simtypes)
i <- 3
cpd.cas <- sim.mol.data(mol.type = "cpd", id.type = cpd.simtypes[2], nmol = 10000)
gene.ensprot <- sim.mol.data(mol.type = "gene", id.type = gene.idtype.list[4], nmol = 50000)
pv.out <- pathview(gene.data = gene.ensprot, cpd.data = cpd.cas, 
    gene.idtype = gene.idtype.list[4], cpd.idtype = cpd.simtypes[2], 
    pathway.id = demo.paths$sel.paths[i], species = "hsa", same.layer = T, 
    out.suffix = "gene.ensprot.cpd.cas", keys.align = "y", kegg.native = T, 
    key.pos = demo.paths$kpos2[i], sign.pos = demo.paths$spos[i], 
    limit = list(gene = 3, cpd = 3), bins = list(gene = 6, cpd = 6))
id.map.cas <- cpdidmap(in.ids = names(cpd.cas), in.type = cpd.simtypes[2], 
    out.type = "KEGG COMPOUND accession")
cpd.kc <- mol.sum(mol.data = cpd.cas, id.map = id.map.cas)
id.map.ensprot <- id2eg(ids = names(gene.ensprot), 
    category = gene.idtype.list[4], org = "Hs")
gene.entrez <- mol.sum(mol.data = gene.ensprot, id.map = id.map.ensprot)
pv.out <- pathview(gene.data = gene.entrez, cpd.data = cpd.kc, 
    pathway.id = demo.paths$sel.paths[i], species = "hsa", same.layer = T, 
    out.suffix = "gene.entrez.cpd.kc", keys.align = "y", kegg.native = T, 
    key.pos = demo.paths$kpos2[i], sign.pos = demo.paths$spos[i], 
    limit = list(gene = 3, cpd = 3), bins = list(gene = 6, cpd = 6))

workflows.name: gage_pathview_pipeline
workflows.intent: Run pathway enrichment analysis using the gage package and automatically visualize the significant pathways using pathview.
input: raw_expression_matrix.tsv (raw or normalized expression matrix with Entrez Gene IDs as row names)
workflows.stages: 1. Load gage and pathview packages ;; 2. Perform pathway analysis using gage ;; 3. Prepare differential expression data ;; 4. Select significant pathways and extract their IDs ;; 5. Visualize the significant pathways using pathview
workflows.code:
library(gage)
library(pathview)
data(gse16873)
cn <- colnames(gse16873)
hn <- grep('HN',cn, ignore.case =TRUE)
dcis <- grep('DCIS',cn, ignore.case =TRUE)
data(kegg.gs)
gse16873.kegg.p <- gage(gse16873, gsets = kegg.gs, ref = hn, samp = dcis)
gse16873.d <- gagePrep(gse16873, ref = hn, samp = dcis)
gse16873.d <- gse16873[,dcis]-gse16873[,hn]
sel <- gse16873.kegg.p$greater[, "q.val"] < 0.1 & !is.na(gse16873.kegg.p$greater[, "q.val"])
path.ids <- rownames(gse16873.kegg.p$greater)[sel]
path.ids2 <- substr(path.ids[c(1, 2, 7)], 1, 8)
pv.out.list <- pathview(gene.data = gse16873.d[, 1:3], pathway.id = path.ids2, species = "hsa")
